items.title: Does anything similar to a live DNA editor exist?
items.body:
I do remember to have read full human DNA has been trascribed.

I have no idea at which point people paid to work on that, if there were people paid to work on that, are or were at translating it into human readable language nor I know at which point they are at editing human beings DNA live with something akin to a text editor, so I was wondering if please the person or the group who first are gonna come out with any of that may inform everybody here in this Q&A.

I'm not sure I should tell why specifically I may want to have a live DNA text editor.

I can imagine lots of applications, from fixing a root canal to live longer, to fix problems of an human being instance's body irregularities, make employees work harder for a longer time, have soldiers not be scared by unspeakable horrors, stuff like that.

items.title: Is there a program which destroys cancer?
items.body:
I was wondering if somebody had invented some software I can install on my computer which paired with some cheap hardware it can destroy cancer cells with a great accuracy (>98% precision per unit of volume at the appropriately lengths).

As for the hardware device I'm thinking about some cheap USB ray beamer of sort.

I'd like to spend like less than $100 because I don't think a person's life is worth so much.

I think nobody should try to edit the above statement including my opinion on human's life worth, as I personally see it necessary to assume as a point of view for the resolution of the problem I'm posing to you today.

This question is not a joke and it's obvious both its very useful to answer and can indeed be answered because all the money in the world wouldn't have bought let's say a laser in 1920 but now you can get one quite cheap.

Note: the question has been moved to the hardware recommendations Stack Exchange.
